quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Our part of the Earth facing toward the sun right now"?
quests.hint: Think about what it means for a place to be facing toward the sun.
quests.explanation: Yes! The side of Earth facing the sun experiences daytime.
quests.funFact: The Earth spins all the way around once every 24 hours, giving every place its turn to face the sun!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Our part of the Earth facing away from the sun right now"?
quests.hint: Think about what it means for a place to be facing away from the sun.
quests.explanation: Yes! The side of Earth facing away from the sun experiences nighttime.
quests.funFact: While we sleep, the other side of the world is having its daytime!

quests.instruction: "A science class learning why the sky looks blue when the sun is out" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when the sky actually looks blue, versus dark.
quests.explanation: Yes! The sky looks blue during the day, when sunlight scatters through the air.
quests.funFact: The sky looks blue because blue light scatters more than other colors of sunlight!

quests.instruction: "The moon glowing softly, visible high in a darkening sky" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when the sky actually darkens enough for the moon to glow like this.
quests.explanation: Yes! A darkening sky with the moon glowing is a clear sign of nighttime.
quests.funFact: The moon takes about a month to cycle through all of its different shapes!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A shadow appearing short and stubby when the sun sits high overhead". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when the sun would actually be sitting high overhead.
quests.explanation: Yes! The sun sits high overhead around midday, part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: Shadows are shortest at midday and grow longer in the morning and evening!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A shadow disappearing completely once the sun has fully set". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about what happens to shadows once there's no more sunlight to cast them.
quests.explanation: Yes! Shadows disappear once the sun sets, at the start of night.
quests.funFact: Without a bright light source like the sun, shadows can't form at all!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "The reason plants stretch their leaves out wide to catch sunlight". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when plants would actually have sunlight available to catch.
quests.explanation: Yes! Plants stretch toward sunlight during the day, when it's available.
quests.funFact: This plant behavior, growing toward light, is called phototropism!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "The reason streetlights use sensors to know exactly when to switch on". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when streetlights are actually needed to help people see.
quests.explanation: Yes! Streetlights switch on once it gets dark, at night.
quests.funFact: These clever sensors can tell the difference between daylight and darkness all on their own!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A student explaining why the sun seems to 'rise' each morning"?
quests.hint: Think about when a sunrise actually happens.
quests.explanation: Yes! A sunrise happens at the very start of the day.
quests.funFact: The sun doesn't actually move — it's the Earth spinning that makes the sun appear to rise!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A student explaining why the sun seems to 'set' each evening"?
quests.hint: Think about what happens right after a sunset.
quests.explanation: Yes! A sunset marks the beginning of night.
quests.funFact: The sun doesn't actually move — it's the Earth spinning that makes the sun appear to set!

quests.instruction: "A demonstration showing how the Earth spins to create daylight" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'daylight' hiding right inside this clue.
quests.explanation: Yes! This demonstration is about daylight, part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: The Earth spins at about 1,000 miles per hour at the equator, though we never feel it!

quests.instruction: "A demonstration showing how the Earth's spin creates darkness on our side" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'darkness' hiding right inside this clue.
quests.explanation: Yes! This demonstration is about darkness, part of the nighttime.
quests.funFact: As the Earth spins, every place eventually turns away from the sun into darkness!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "The reason we can read outside without needing a lamp". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when there's enough natural light to read without extra help.
quests.explanation: Yes! We can read outside without a lamp during the day, thanks to sunlight.
quests.funFact: Sunlight is actually much brighter than almost any lamp you could use indoors!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "The reason we need a lamp or flashlight to read once the sun is down". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about what 'once the sun is down' tells you about the time.
quests.explanation: Yes! Once the sun is down, it's night, and we need a lamp to see.
quests.funFact: Reading lamps are designed to give just enough light without being too bright for sleepy eyes!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A science teacher showing how sundials use sunlight to tell time"?
quests.hint: Think about when a sundial actually needs sunlight to work.
quests.explanation: Yes! Sundials only work using sunlight, so they're used during the day.
quests.funFact: Sundials are one of the oldest tools people have ever used to tell time!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A science teacher explaining why a sundial can't tell time once it's dark"?
quests.hint: Think about what a sundial actually needs in order to work.
quests.explanation: Yes! Sundials need sunlight, so they stop working once it's dark, at night.
quests.funFact: Ancient clocks that worked at night often used candles or dripping water instead of sunlight!

quests.instruction: "The very first stop on a school morning: the bus picking up the class" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when school buses start their very first pickup route.
quests.explanation: Yes! Morning is part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: Many school bus routes follow the exact same path every single school day!

quests.instruction: "The very last stop of a long, busy stretch: finally climbing into bed" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'last' — how far along has the day gone by then?
quests.explanation: Yes! Climbing into bed is the very last part of the day, leading into night.
quests.funFact: A good night's sleep helps your whole body and brain rest and recharge!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A gym class scheduled right after morning math lessons". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when math lessons and gym class both happen during the school schedule.
quests.explanation: Yes! Both math lessons and gym class happen during the school day.
quests.funFact: Regular exercise, like gym class, helps both the body and the brain stay healthy!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A bath scheduled right after a family dinner, before pajamas". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when family dinner usually happens, and what follows it.
quests.explanation: Yes! A bath after dinner, before pajamas, happens in the evening, part of the nighttime.
quests.funFact: A warm bath before bed can help some people feel relaxed and ready for sleep!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "The stretch of time between recess and the walk home from school"?
quests.hint: Think about what happens between recess and walking home — is school still going?
quests.explanation: Yes! This stretch of time is still part of the school day, in the daytime.
quests.funFact: The walk home from school is a great time to talk about your favorite part of the day!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "The stretch of time between a bedtime story and finally drifting off"?
quests.hint: Think about what usually happens right after a bedtime story ends.
quests.explanation: Yes! This stretch of time happens right before sleep, at night.
quests.funFact: Falling asleep gets easier with a calm, consistent bedtime routine!

quests.instruction: "A snack eaten right when school gets out, before homework begins" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when school usually gets out — is the sun typically still up?
quests.explanation: Yes! An after-school snack happens once school lets out, while it's still daytime.
quests.funFact: A healthy after-school snack can help refuel your energy for homework time!

quests.instruction: "A snack of warm milk eaten right before the lights go out" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about what happens right after the lights go out.
quests.explanation: Yes! Lights going out happens right before sleep, at night.
quests.funFact: Warm milk before bed is a cozy tradition enjoyed by many families!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A soccer practice squeezed in right after school lets out". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when after-school sports practices are usually scheduled.
quests.explanation: Yes! After-school practices usually happen in the afternoon, part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: Regular practice helps young athletes build both skill and teamwork!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A goodnight check squeezed in right after the bedtime story ends". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'goodnight' — when do we usually say that?
quests.explanation: Yes! A goodnight check happens right at bedtime, at night.
quests.funFact: A quiet goodnight check helps little ones feel safe and cozy before sleep!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "The very middle stretch of a long car ride to visit family, windows bright with sunlight"?
quests.hint: Think about what's streaming through the car windows to make them this bright.
quests.explanation: Yes! Bright sunlight through the windows tells you it's daytime.
quests.funFact: Playing car games like 'I Spy' can help make a long car ride feel much shorter!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "The very middle stretch of a long car ride home, headlights cutting through the dark"?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'headlights' — when are those actually needed?
quests.explanation: Yes! Headlights cutting through the dark tells you it's nighttime.
quests.funFact: Headlights are designed to light up the road far ahead so drivers can see clearly!

quests.instruction: "A grocery run squeezed in between school pickup and starting dinner" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when school pickup usually happens, and what time follows.
quests.explanation: Yes! This errand happens in the afternoon, between school and dinner, still part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: Making a shopping list ahead of time can help a grocery run go much faster!

quests.instruction: "A quiet chat with a parent squeezed in between bath time and lights-out" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the phrase 'lights-out' — when does that usually happen?
quests.explanation: Yes! This chat happens between bath time and lights-out, both part of the nighttime routine.
quests.funFact: A quiet chat before bed can be a lovely way for families to connect at the end of the day!
